Thanks Sarah — great, and thanks Tom for jumping in.

Tom/Network team — a few practical notes and what we typically see on Private VPC deployments: 

1) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering (summary):
   - PrivateLink: single-sided vended endpoint, no cross-account route table changes, easier from a networking change control perspective. Latency is typically on par for most workloads; good when you need strict network isolation and simple ops.
   - VPC Peering: direct routing between VPCs; can be simpler if you need very high throughput and lower hop counts, but requires managing route tables and CIDR planning.

2) IP allowlists & egress:
   - For Private deployments we offer two options: a managed set of static egress IPs you can allow, or configuring a VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) so traffic never traverses the public internet. If you want a fully deterministic allowlist, PrivateLink + endpoint is the recommended approach.
   - Example shortlist of IPs (for allowlist testing): 52.10.34.12, 52.10.34.13, 52.10.34.14 (these are sample/elastic NAT egress addresses we assign during setup; we will provide final ranges prior to cutover).

3) Data plane encryption & certs:
   - All connections are TLS1.2+; we can support mutual TLS if required.

4) Perf considerations:
   - For your stated 25 req/sec steady with bursts to 150 req/sec, either option will work; peering can give slightly lower tail latency in some AWS regions under high concurrency. We'll validate with a quick perf test during the pilot.

Proposed next steps:

- If you can, please fill out the attached checklist; Monica will run the network-runbook review with your team.
